idea: labeler/prompt variants (labeler-level agreement with gold dev)
change: deepseek-v4.1-flash hard vs soft (distribution) vs soft+20 seeds vs soft+seeds+HelpSteer2 rubric guidance; qwen3.7-flash and gemini-2.5-flash-lite soft+seeds+guide
takeaway: all labelers ~0.40 on dev; soft/seeds +0.02-0.03 (within noise, dev halves differ by up to 0.3 on helpfulness); rubric guidance did not help; gemini-lite poor; soft output ~2x cost so unaffordable for the pool

idea: compact decimal-rating labeler (one fractional 0-4 score per attribute, cheap output)
change: custom prompt (label_dec.py); flash and qwen, with/without seeds
takeaway: qwen decimal no-seed costs 4.5e-5/call (1/3 of flash hard), labeler-level 0.379; seeds help qwen but cost 3x

idea: labeler ensembles (average of expected scores), labeler level on dev
takeaway: ensembling two cheap labelers +0.04 at labeler level; but see student results: did NOT transfer to the student

idea: CPU latency of gte-modernbert int8 ONNX vs sequence length and depth (untrained, batch 1, 4 threads, loaded machine)
takeaway: full inputs (median 430, p95 ~1000 tokens) are 10x over the gate; need ~128 tokens at full depth or truncated depth

idea: shared encoder, 5 heads, response-preserving truncation + length header, depth vs token budget (v1 flash silver 4.9k, hard labels, ordinal smoothing 0.6)
change: L22@128 vs L11@192 vs L8@256 vs L6@320 tokens
takeaway: one-pass 5-head model with a length header ('prompt N response M lines K') at 128 tokens already matches/exceeds v1; depth matters more than extra tokens

idea: seed variance of the baseline (L22@128, v1 silver)
takeaway: seed noise ~0.01; dev sampling noise larger (~0.03)

idea: one-hot targets instead of ordinal smoothing
takeaway: no gain from one-hot; keep sigma 0.6

idea: rule-based degraded variants with known direction (response from another prompt -> help/corr 0; response truncated to 25-45% -> lower)
change: +1460 synthetic pairs on top of 4.9k silver
takeaway: hurt: real low scores come from subtle factual/instruction errors, not irrelevance or truncation; synthetic shortcuts mislead

idea: int8 dynamic quantisation: which MatMuls
change: all weight MatMuls int8 vs keeping mlp.Wo (and head) fp32
takeaway: mlp.Wo has activation outliers: quantising it costs 0.04 dev; keeping it fp32 restores fp32 accuracy (agreement 0.997)

idea: post-hoc stacking: ridge from 5 head scores to each gold attribute (5-fold CV on dev)
takeaway: 200 dev examples too few to fit 5x5 stacking weights

idea: fixed h/c blend: helpfulness and correctness heads both output the mean of their expected scores (gold r=0.95)
takeaway: +0.01 consistently on every model and both dev halves

idea: qwen decimal labels for the whole pool (20.1k) as more/cheaper data
change: qwen on 20.1k pool; flash+qwen merged where both
takeaway: student trained on qwen labels is much worse (0.28-0.29) than on flash (0.35) although labeler-level dev was similar; merging hurts too: labeler agreement with gold does not predict student quality

idea: labeler-specific heads: 5 heads on flash labels + 5 auxiliary heads on qwen labels (shared encoder), deploy flash heads
takeaway: qwen as auxiliary task neither helps nor hurts much; less stable than flash-only

idea: more flash labels via cheapest OpenRouter provider (provider.sort=price)
takeaway: cheapest route costs 5.3e-5/call vs 1.4e-4 via throughput routing; +2.4k flash labels gave +0.01

idea: epochs and depth on flash 7.3k
takeaway: 3 epochs best (overfits later); removing 4 layers costs ~0.04 dev, so keep 22 layers at 128 tokens

idea: per-layer sensitivity of mlp.Wo int8 (quantise one layer at a time)
change: keep mlp.Wo fp32 only in sensitive layers 4,9,11,15; int8 elsewhere
takeaway: outliers concentrate in mlp.Wo of layers 4/9/11/15 (single-layer agreement 0.92-0.985 vs 0.993 elsewhere); selective fp32 is a latency/accuracy middle ground

idea: train on gold dev+seeds too (weight 5) alongside 7.3k flash labels; estimated by 5-fold CV on dev (fixed 3 epochs)
change: +160 dev (other folds) + 20 seeds per fold, gold_w=5
takeaway: +0.012-0.015 (not significant), concentrated in helpfulness/correctness (+0.04): human labels teach the quality notion the LLM labels miss

idea: ORT transformer graph optimizer (bert fusions: SkipLayerNorm, Gelu) before int8
takeaway: fusions did not reduce batch-1 latency on this CPU; accuracy unchanged

idea: ORT session options (dynamic_block_base 2/4, denormals-as-zero)
takeaway: within noise

idea: shorter token budget (96-112 vs 128) at 22 layers
takeaway: at batch 1 below ~128 tokens latency is dominated by per-layer overhead, so only depth buys latency, and depth costs accuracy (L18: -0.04 dev)

idea: gold weight 20 instead of 5 (5-fold CV on dev)
takeaway: heavier gold weighting does not add; keep w=5

idea: post-test diagnostic: does a labelled sibling response (same prompt) in training inflate dev Spearman?
change: split dev into 105 examples whose prompt has a flash-labelled sibling in training vs 95 without
takeaway: no prompt-sibling leakage effect; the dev(0.388 CV)->test gap on helpfulness/correctness is dev noise (n=200, SE~0.07/attribute) and/or train-vs-validation shift, not leakage

idea: stronger labelers for helpfulness/correctness only (2-question prompt, no seeds), labeler-level agreement with gold dev
change: flash no-reasoning / flash reasoning low / flash reasoning medium / deepseek-v4-pro / claude-haiku-5.5 (+reasoning 1k) / gemini-3.1-flash-lite reasoning
takeaway: enabling deepseek-flash reasoning is the best value: +0.07/+0.03 over non-reasoning flash at 1.2e-4/call; pro without reasoning is worse than flash; Jev reference 0.400/0.369

idea: pairwise logistic ranking loss on same-prompt pairs (1,376 flash-labelled pairs), flash 7.3k, no gold, fixed 3 epochs
takeaway: ranking loss does not help (mean 0.350/0.338 vs 0.364); only ~2.7k of 7.3k rows are in pairs and within-pair LLM label differences are noisy

idea: student probe: flash-with-reasoning h/c labels vs original flash h/c labels on the same 1.5k pool examples (students trained only on those rows, 3 seeds each, 4 epochs, L22@128)
change: hc_override with reasoning labels vs original labels
takeaway: reasoning labels agree better with gold (+0.07/+0.03 labeler-level) but the student does not improve: same pattern as qwen; the 128-token student cannot see the evidence the reasoning labeler used

idea: diagnostic: same reasoning-vs-original h/c probe with 512-token inputs (ignoring latency) to test whether truncation hides the evidence
takeaway: 512 tokens neither helps the student nor makes reasoning labels useful at 1.5k rows; truncation is not the (only) bottleneck, the encoder does not learn factual/instruction checking from ~1-7k LLM labels

idea: flash labels (v1 prompt, cheapest route) on the remaining 12.8k pool -> 20.1k flash labels (round-1 recipe data x2.7)
change: +12,766 flash hard labels; students without gold, 2 seeds, fixed 3 epochs vs 7.3k (F7)
takeaway: more flash labels do not help (complexity/verbosity slightly up, h/c down); the round-2 gold-CV runs were stopped since the no-gold comparison already ruled out a dev win; no round-2 test scoring

idea: relaxed setting: longest input that fits the 70 ms p95 gate on 8 threads (round-1 model, int8, batch 1)
takeaway: 8 threads buys only ~10-20% at batch 1 on this 10-core CPU: 144 tokens already exceeds the gate (p95 75 ms), so the longest fitting input is still 128 tokens; the relaxed recipe is identical to round 1 and was not trained or re-scored (the 512-token probe in round 2 also showed no dev gain)

idea: relaxed: round-1 recipe at 192 input tokens (fits 8-thread gate only on a quiet machine: p95 63 ms quiet, 100 ms loaded)
change: budget 128 -> 192, 3 seeds, no gold, fixed 3 epochs, h/c blend; vs 128 tokens 3 seeds
takeaway: longer input is worse on dev (h/c significantly); consistent with the 512-token probe; no relaxed re-scoring
